title: Visualizing Cellular Dynamics and Protein Localization in 3D Collagen
protocol: Reconstitute cryovial(s) of PBMCs by placing them in a 37°C water bath.
Add warmed media to the partially thawed cell suspension at a 1:9 ratio and place into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge cell suspension for 10 minutes at 400 × g at 20°C–22°C.
Decant supernatant and add 10 mL of fresh complete RPMI media.
Repeat the centrifugation step two more times.
Count cells and assess viability using trypan blue; ideal viability is 80% or higher.
Resuspend cells with EasySep Buffer at a concentration of 50 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Perform negative selection to isolate naive CD4 T cells using the EasySep human naive CD4 T cell isolation kit, following manufacturer’s protocol.
Decant selected T cells into a 15 mL conical tube.
Wash with 5 mL complete RPMI medium.
Count isolated CD4+ T cells using a hemocytometer.
Resuspend cells at 106 cells/mL in complete RPMI medium.
Pipette 1 mL of the cell suspension into each well of a 24 well plate (106 T cells per well).
Add 25 μL of anti-CD3ε/CD28 antibody-coated Dynabeads to each well and mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Place culture plate in the 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for 48 hours.
Remove beads by placing cell suspension in a 5 mL Falcon tube and placing it into the EasySep magnet (STEMCELL technologies) for 2 minutes.
Carefully decant T cells into a fresh 15 mL conical tube.
Wash with 3 mL of complete RPMI media.
Count cells after washing.
Adjust cell concentration to 0.1–0.2 × 106 cells/mL in complete RPMI medium with 8 ng/mL recombinant human (rh) IL-2 into a T25 or T75 flask, standing up.
Change media on day 5.
Re-adjust cell concentration to 106 cells/mL in complete RPMI medium + 8 ng/mL rh IL-2.
Thaw out cryovial(s) of frozen PBMCs by placing them in the 37°C water bath.
Once partially thawed, add warmed media to the cell suspension and place into a 50 mL conical tube at a 1:9 ratio (1 mL cells:9 mL RPMI medium).
Centrifuge PBMCs at 500 × g at 20°C–22°C for 10 minutes.
Decant supernatant and add 10 mL of fresh complete RPMI media.
Repeat the process twice and count cells using a hemocytometer.
Resuspend PBMCs at 100 × 10^6 cells/mL in EasySep Buffer.
Perform a positive selection for CD14+ monocytes using the EasySep human CD14 positive selection kit, following manufacturer’s protocol.
Resuspend monocytes at 1–2 × 10^6 cells/mL in complete RPMI media supplemented with 50 ng/mL of rhGM-CSF and 50 ng/mL rhIL-4.
Place cells in a T25 or T75 ultra-low attachment NuncSphera flask and place the flask in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Collect and centrifuge cells at 400 × g for 10 minutes on Day 2.
Resuspend cells in fresh complete RPMI media + 50 ng/mL of rhGM-CSF and 50 ng/mL rhIL-4.
Maintain cell concentrations at 1–2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Return flasks to the incubator.
On Day 5, perform phenotypic analysis using anti-CD11c, CD80, CD86, and MHC-II antibodies where immature MDDCs are characterized as CD11c+CD80lowCD86lowMHC-IIlow.
Resuspend cells at 0.8 × 10^6 cells/mL in complete RPMI medium supplemented with 25 ng/mL rhGM-CSF, 25 ng/mL rhIL-4, and 100 ng/mL of LPS (S. Minnesota) for 24 hours to obtain mature MDDCs.
Perform phenotypic analysis by flow cytometry at this point to confirm maturation characterized by upregulation of CD80, CD86, and MHC-II expression.
Count each cell type, centrifuge and resuspend in 1 mL of sterile cell staining buffer (1% FCS in PBS) at a maximum concentration of 10^7/mL in a 15 mL conical falcon tube.
Determine the ideal amount of T cells and DCs to stain in a single tube, typically 4 million T cells and 8 million DCs respectively.
Make a 1 mL solution of Celltracker dye at 2× concentration with pre-warmed staining buffer and place in a 15 mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension and mix well by pipetting up and down.
Place cells in a 37°C water bath for 15–20 min.
Underlay cell suspension with 2 mL of ice-cold 100% FCS, resulting in two distinct liquid phases.
Centrifuge cells at 400 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate out the culture supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend in 10 mL of complete RPMI media and centrifuge again at 400 × g for 5 min.
Assemble the chamber slides by placing the adhesive silicone isolators onto a microscope glass slide.
Peel the adhesive from the top and adhere a 18 × 18 mm cover slip, leaving a 2–3 mm gap at one end.
Ensure that there are no bubbles/holes for the collagen mixture to leak from.
Prepare collagen gel mixture in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf or 5 mL FACS tube.
Mix all reagents quickly at 20–22°C with cold reagents to prevent premature gel solidification.
Mix the collagen solution by pipetting up and down without introducing bubbles.
Add the cell suspension to the collagen solution and mix gently without forming bubbles.
Carefully pipette the mixture into each slide chamber through the gap created with the cover slip.
Place the chambers in the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2, standing them vertically.
Allow the gel to polymerize for 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Check that the collagen gels have solidified and appear opaque with a pinkish orange color.
Place collagen gel slides onto a heated platform.
Plug heating resistors into the temperature controller.
Ensure the temperature is maintained at 37°C using a thermocouple.
Turn on two-photon femtosecond lasers.
Adjust lasers to the optimal wavelength for maximal excitation of Celltracker dye or fluorescent protein.
Use wavelengths between 780–830 nm for excitation.
Acquire images using a 20× water-immersion objective lens.
Select image acquisition parameters.
Record time-lapse images using 13 z-stacks at 4 μm spacing.
Acquire data for 30 seconds per cycle over 121 total cycles.
Optimize acquisition parameters for each experiment to balance data sufficiency and cytotoxic effects from imaging.
Transduce cells with lentivirus-expressing fluorescent proteins as an alternative to fluorescent dyes.
Isolate cells from fluorescent reporter transgenic mice if available.
Determine optimal voltage settings on the temperature controller for each heating platform before starting the experiment.
Use a thermocouple to ensure the collagen matrix gel is maintained at 37°C ± 0.5°C by inserting the probe into the gel.
Convert the original .xml file into .ims file using the Imaris FileConverter Software.
Open the .ims file in the Imaris 8.2 software.
Open Image Properties under the Edit tab and correct minimum X, Y, and Z values to 0.
Adjust the Voxel size for the z value used to acquire the images.
Under the Time Point section, select the “All Equidistant” tab and adjust the Time Interval to the experimental time period.
Press “Fit” at the bottom left corner of the program if the image disappears.
Select “Add new Spots” (Orange circles) to start tracking T cells over time.
Input algorithm instructions and press next.
Select a small region of interest to implement the algorithm, choose which channel to analyze, and specify the approximate XY diameter.
Adjust the detection intensity by sliding the highlighted bar to ensure that only one cell is spotted at any one time.
Ensure each spot locates at the cell body.
Delete cell tracks where the entire cell is not in the field of view from the analysis.
Select the cell track in question by selecting the Edit tracks tab.
Inspect each cell track and ensure they accurately depict the same cell over time.
Manually connect separate tracks belonging to the same cell by selecting two objects while holding the command/control key and pressing “Connect.”
Combine two separate tracks into a single cell track.
Visually inspect all cell tracks for accuracy.
Select the statistics tab to export all cell migration parameters as an excel file after completing cell tracking.
Embed cells of interest into collagen according to detailed instructions provided above.
Prepare a total volume of 540 μL of cell:collagen mixture with no more than 3 million total cells.
Dispense 540 μL of the cell:collagen suspension into each well of a 24 well plate, creating a cell bubble in each well.
Place the culture plate containing the collagen gels in a 37°C incubator to allow solidification.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed 4% paraformaldehyde in 5% sucrose solution to each well after the desired incubation time.
Incubate plates with paraformaldehyde solution for 24 hours at 37°C.
Warm fixation buffer to 37°C for 30 min.
Quickly add the warmed fixation buffer to collagen gels while in the incubator.
Remove PFA solution from the gel and wash with PBS containing 0.2% Tween-20 three times, each for 5 min.
Aspirate washing buffer carefully.
Add 2 ml of 0.15 M glycine buffer (pH 7) to quench excess PFA by placing it in the 4°C fridge for 18–24 h.
Rinse gels with wash buffer three times and aspirate using a pipette.
Permeabilize cells by adding 2 ml of 0.5% Triton X solution, incubating for 48 h in the fridge.
Rinse gels with wash buffer three times and aspirate carefully.
Add 2 ml of 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS to reduce non-specific binding by antibodies, leaving it for 18–24 h in the 4°C fridge.
Rinse gels with wash solution three times.
Transfer each collagen gel block into a new 24-well culture dish using a plastic spoon.
Add 300-500 μl of 1.65 μM Texas red conjugated phalloidin solution to cover the entire gel, according to manufacturer’s recommendation.
Incubate gels for 24 h in the dark at 4°C fridge.
Rinse gels with wash buffer three times, 5 min per wash.
Gently aspirate buffer from the gels using a pipette.
Place the gels onto a glass microscope slide using a plastic spoon.
Remove excess liquid from around the gels using a Kimwipe.
Surround each gel with vacuum grease to create an airtight seal.
Apply enough grease to match the height of the gel.
Place PBS into the grease well and gently place a coverslip on top of the gel, slightly pushing down on the grease ring to form a seal.
Inject additional PBS using an insulin syringe to remove large air bubbles from the preparation.
Collect 3D stack images of the mounted gels under the microscope.
Recommend taking z-stack spacing of 1–2 μm for 3D cell reconstruction.
Import images into Imaris software or other image analysis software for expression/localization analysis.
